proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived candidate matched finite-p welfare-regret bounds, a total dyadic learner, same-law propensity comparator, and an ambient inclusion converse. D0.5 stopped at a subfield novelty ceiling below the field floor, with weighted projection cross terms and the mixed-variance ledger unreproduced. No formalization was launched; the upper, two-sided frontier and no-log headline remain uncertified, without a definitive falsity finding.
tldr: Original conditional-mean treatment allocation has the matched finite-sample regret order \(r_n(v)=n^{-(1+\kappa)\min\{\gamma q/(\gamma+q),\,2S/(1+S/\gamma+2\alpha+\beta/q)\}}\) on \(\mathcal M_v\), with no critical logarithm. A total observable learner returns a finite growing dyadic tree and a public \(90\%\) certificate for actual regret. The same-law supplied-propensity comparison gives the exact survival boundary, including equality. Strict inclusion in the numerical published ambient class transfers the welfare converse upward as \(W_n^{\mathcal K}(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\ge W_n(v)\ge c_vr_n(v)\). This ambient transfer is one-sided.
gap: Bonvini, Kennedy and Keele supply the closest causal sign-loss result, while Kennedy et al. identify the nuisance-smoothness obstruction for CATE. The verified statements do not determine its survival under arbitrary conditional finite moments on the exact uniform design.
fill: The output is an explicit finite-sample regret order with whole-class attainment and an all-randomized-learner converse, together with the same-law revelation comparison. Projection and likelihood handles preserve the original allocation task. A growing dyadic realization accounts for approximation to the unrestricted sign oracle.
